steps.name: Javier
steps.text: This is the only intact salt ship left. The rest have taken damage, but there are plenty of salvageable parts.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: These are the blueprints, along with notes on their operations. And here's a map of the Salt Flat.

steps.name: Excited Merchant
steps.text: I'll take everything! Think of the time we'll save if we can travel straight through the Salt Flat!

steps.name: Excited Merchant
steps.text: Name your price!

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: Here. Gold doblones only, no credit.

steps.name: Excited Merchant
steps.text: Deal!

steps.name: Excited Merchant
steps.text: Here you go. Is this enough?

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: Looks correct to me.

steps.name: Excited Merchant
steps.text: Well then, I'll be going! Have a good day, señores.

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: He didn't even hesitate... Did we ask for too little?

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: One second!

steps.name: Excited Merchant
steps.text: Er... is something the matter?
Javier catches up and climbs up the deck by rope.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: I want to keep this helm wheel! How much? I'll pay you back.

steps.name: Merchant
steps.text: The helm wheel, of all things? It's the most important part of the ship.

steps.name: Merchant
steps.text: Well, if you really want it—

steps.name: Merchant
steps.text: I'll part with it for this much.

steps.name: Merchant
steps.text: Now now, don't give that look! We had a deal. It's my ship now, right?

spans.text: Now now, don't give that look! We had a deal. It's

steps.name: Merchant
steps.text: We do honest business here. It's only a question of whether you think it's worth the price!

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: Never mind then...

steps.name: Excited Merchant
steps.text: How unfortunate. Well, I hope to do business with you again!

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: Sailors! Roll call!

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: Here's the cash from selling the salt ship. Everyone gets an equal share.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: Do whatever you want with it.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: Here's your share, Rus.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: Not sure what I wanna do with it.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: Just make a choice. It's not hard.

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: ...I wanted to leave Juana for stability. Then you turned out to be just as loco, so I figured we'd never have peace under you.

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: And now I'm in this town, looking at the folks here, all thin and gaunt, their eyes like dead fins... This what peace looks like?

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: And if I go anywhere else, how can I live a decent life when I've only ever been a pirate?

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: Go ahead and laugh, but I admire Teach. She's just a few years older, but she knows what she wants.

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: When I saw her make up her mind to go with Juana, even with all those injuries... I wouldn't have had the guts.

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: Well, forget me, what about you?

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: Probably go somewhere else, open a restaurant.

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: Well... if that's what you want. I'm just gonna finish this smoke and get going.

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: Who can say for sure where the future lies, right?
Javier watches as the white sail of the salt ship disappears in the distance, as does Rus's silhouette.
He puts his own share in his pocket, and walks down the road.

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: How much for this?

steps.name: Caravan Trader
steps.text: One silver piece.

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: What about this?

steps.name: Caravan Trader
steps.text: Same.

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: Hey, that's not half bad!

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: I'll have this, this, and this. Put 'em on my car, the one behind me.

steps.name: Caravan Trader
steps.text: Sure thing! Where are you heading, with all this stuff?

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: I just bought whatever I wanted. What's wrong with that?

steps.name: Caravan Trader
steps.text: Oh, nothing at all! Just tell me if you want anything else, and I'll load it up for you!

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: That's more like it.

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: Clothes, accessories, trinkets... Feels like I'm still missing something.

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: But what?

steps.name: Caravanner A
steps.text: (Whisper) ...Yeah, crazy, right?

steps.name: Caravanner B
steps.text: (Whisper) How was I supposed to know it'd turn out like that? Good heavens...

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: (Hey, that buckle on his belt looks pretty nice... and shiny...)

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: (Is it metal? Or gemstone? I want it...)

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: (I want it so bad...)

steps.name: Caravanner A
steps.text: (Whisper) ...They found it on the road and decided to dig it up. Thought it might fetch a few coins...

steps.name: Caravanner B
steps.text: (Whisper) They found a buyer? I can't believe it...

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: (They haven't noticed me. And it's right there...)

steps.name: Caravanner A
steps.text: (Whisper) ...Can you believe they offered THAT much? Enough to set you up for life!

steps.name: Caravanner B
steps.text: (Whisper) Is that why we're heading that way?

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: (Got it!)

steps.name: Caravanner A
steps.text: (Whisper) Yeah... we'll make it big in Columbia...

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: (Make it big?)
Pascuala lets go, and the buckle falls back onto the man's belt.

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: What do you mean, make it big?

steps.name: Caravanner A & B
steps.text: Whoa!

steps.name: Caravanner A
steps.text: Were you eavesdropping?

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: Hehe.

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: I wouldn't have said anything if it were anyone else, but you two look pretty smart to me. A cut above the rest, you might say.

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: Which is why I mustered the courage to speak up.

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: Here's my fare. It's a long way to Columbia, so why don't you tell me more about it on the way?

steps.name: Teach
steps.text: Are we really going out to sea, señora?

steps.name: Teach
steps.text: Can't believe I lived to see the day...

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: Of course we are, Perlita. We're heading out to sea.

steps.name: Teach
steps.text: Incredible...
Juana brushes her windswept hair and looks behind her.

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: Now we really have nothing left, Isidro, but my mind is set.

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: Will you be coming with us?

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: Señora Juana...

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: Will you be my first mate?

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: Well. Alright then, captain, I'm ready to... huh?

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: It seems my old friend is a little grumpy... Let's see if we can cheer her up.

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: Hm...

steps.name: Teach
steps.text: Mm...

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: I suppose the new energy system is a bit much for a decades-old transmission core...

steps.name: Teach
steps.text: Hmm... Weedy already went back in her modified boat. Guess we'll have to fix it ourselves. What materials do we got?

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: Isidro, what's in that bulky bag you have there?

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: Things Elysium gave me. I'm not sure how helpful they'll be...

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: Well, open it up and we'll find out.
Isidro opens his backpack, and the contents spill out.
Juana and Teach lean forward and examine them.

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: Vitamins? Certainly useful at sea.

steps.name: Teach
steps.text: And so are the radio equipment and waterproof boots...

steps.name: Teach
steps.text: These tools... they'll come in handy with the repairs.

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: Looks like we owe him one. None of these things would be easy to find out here.

steps.name: Teach
steps.text: I'm taking these two. Might be able to fix the problem.

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: By the look on your face, I take it you didn't know? Did he hand you all this on the day we said goodbye?

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: No... we didn't say goodbye that day.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: He's been giving me things from time to time since a while ago. I just stuffed everything into a bag.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: He knew.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: Even before I did.

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: Of course he knew. He's your best buddy, isn't he?

steps.name: Teach
steps.text: Fixed it!

steps.name: Eager Sailor
steps.text: We ready then? We can set sail?

steps.name: Excited Sailor
steps.text: Hey ho—

steps.name: Excited Sailor
steps.text: We're sailin'! We're sailin'!

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: Let's go, captain. It's time to set a course.
Isidro takes the spyglass from Juana.
Grains of salt stir upon the Flat like white waves, but he soon turns his eyes from that false sea to the sky on the horizon, to that one little streak of bright blue.
Standing on the bow by himself, he reaches out with his arm, and waits for the whirling light upon it to point the way.
He stands on the street, putting his palms together. The last speck of stardust has disappeared, and darkness takes over once again.

steps.name: Shy Child
steps.text: The fireworks is over? Is it time to go?

steps.name: Surprised Passerby
steps.text: Let's go. Time to go home.

steps.name: Aloof Passerby
steps.text: Hmph...
The onlookers disperse. The crowd that had gathered because of him have left him again.
Receiving no answer from him, Juana steps forward, with Teach following behind her on the front deck.
One by one, the sailors gather, trying to see what their new captain is seeing.
A crowd forms around Isidro. Those who have fallen behind have to strain their necks and force their way through.

steps.name: Curious Sailor
steps.text: What is it, captain? What do you see?

steps.name: Anxious Sailor
steps.text: Have you found which way to go?

steps.name: Doubting Sailor
steps.text: Which way is the sea? Are we sailing in the right direction?
Isidro does not answer. His entire attention is focused upon his arm.

steps.name: Doubting Sailor
steps.text: Why's it spinning?

steps.name: Anxious Sailor
steps.text: How long does this take? Where're we going?

steps.name: Curious Sailor
steps.text: Ah... where will we go from here?

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: Patience, patience. Our captain will tell us the answer.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: Now...

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: Which way do we go?
At his question, the light on his arm converges, pointing towards the horizon, straight and firm.
He longs to sail towards the boundless ocean together with his friends. Thus, the Corazonix points out the direction for him.
Sailors cheer, rum is spilled—

steps.name: Excited Sailor
steps.text: Over yonder!

steps.name: Eager Sailor
steps.text: The sea!
All eyes are upon Isidro.

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: Give the order, captain.
The sailors already have ropes in hand. Juana's hand is on the helm, waiting for his command.
Isidro takes a deep breath and takes in the eager eyes gazing upon him, filled with hopes and expectations, burdens that he is no longer afraid to bear.
He feels the wind of the Salt Flat. His shoulders are light.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: Ahoy, sailors!

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: Anchors aweigh, hoist the sails—

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: —We sail out to sea!

steps.name: Sailors
steps.text: To sea—

steps.name: Sailors
steps.text: Hey—Ho—!♪

a.text: High winds roar, our clothes a-tore♪
Rain drowns our drunken haze, and lights our hearts ablaze♪
Ready, ho! Sail forth! A thousand ships break port!♪

steps.name: Thrilled Sailor
steps.text: I will wrestle the waves! I will sail the winds! I will fence the lightning—

steps.name: Eager Sailor
steps.text: I want to find the treasures buried at the bottom of the sea! All that shiny gold!

steps.name: Hesitant Sailor
steps.text: You know... I've been thinking... we all came together because we want to go out to sea...

steps.name: Hesitant Sailor
steps.text: So would we split up again if we have different ideas?

steps.name: Teach
steps.text: You're thinking that far ahead, chaval?

steps.name: Teach
steps.text: Whatever the future holds, we're together now, and we're going out to sea!

steps.name: Teach
steps.text: So stop thinking too much and grab that rope!

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: Got some rum for you, Captain Isidro! Say something!
Isidro stands atop the bow. He can feel the air grow moist. It is an exciting feeling.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: Into the distance.
...Mmph...
...Mmph... mmph...

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: What's that familiar sound?
...Mmph...

steps.name: Nene
steps.text: Mreep!

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: Nene?!

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: Nene! You're alive!

steps.name: Nene
steps.text: (Eagerly licks Juana's cheeks)

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: Aww...

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: Are you coming out to sea with us?

steps.name: Nene
steps.text: (Bounces around excitedly)

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: Oh, my sweet baby!
A trail of blood leads from the steam to the depths of the boundless Salt Flat.
A cold tongue tastes the blood in the mouth. Broken limbs keep crawling, driven by a powerful desire that lives on without its master.
A short distance away, an appendage breaks through the salt layer, wiggling towards a sunlight it has not seen for many years. Then, a second, a third...
It is another powerful desire without a master, compelling the light-emitting organ to reach for the sun, as though trying to gain the sun's light.
All he wants is to live on. All it wants is to live on.
By whatever means. In whatever form.
The broken parts of Man and Seaborn struggle, wiggle, hungrily devouring each other.
They will walk this land in perpetuity.
